sections.theory:
Example 7.2

A random sample of 25 hens from a normal population showed that the average laying is 250 eggs per year. The company claims that the average laying is 285 eggs per year with a standard deviation of 25 eggs per year. Test the claim of the company against the alternative that average laying is less than 285 eggs at α = 0.05

Solution:

i. H_0:\mu=285

H_1:\mu<285

ii. α = 0.05

iii. Test statistic: As n = 25 is small but σ is known, therefore, we use test statistic for μ as Z=\frac{\overline{X}-\mu}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}}

iv. Computation:

Given n = 25, \overline{X}=250, σ = 25

$Z=\frac{250-285}{25/\sqrt{25}}=\frac{-35}{25/5}=\frac{-35}{5}=-7$

v. Critical region:

Given α = 0.05 since we have one tailed test, so 0.5 − 0.05 = 0.4500. Make inverse use of area table we have Z_\alpha=Z_{0.05}=1.645 i.e. reject H_0 if Z calculated is less than or equal to −1.645.

vi. Conclusion:

Since our calculated value of Z lies in the rejection region, therefore, we reject H_0 and accept H_1.

مثال 7.2

حل:

i. H_0:\mu=285

H_1:\mu<285

ii. α = 0.05

iii. جانچ کا شماریہ: چونکہ n = 25 چھوٹا ہے لیکن σ معلوم ہے، لہٰذا ہم μ کے لیے یہ جانچ کا شماریہ استعمال کرتے ہیں Z=\frac{\overline{X}-\mu}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}}

iv. حساب:

دیا گیا ہے n = 25، \overline{X}=250، σ = 25

$Z=\frac{250-285}{25/\sqrt{25}}=\frac{-35}{25/5}=\frac{-35}{5}=-7$

v. فیصلہ کن علاقہ:

دیا گیا ہے α = 0.05، چونکہ ہماری یک طرفہ جانچ ہے، لہٰذا 0.5 − 0.05 = 0.4500۔ رقبے کے جدول کا الٹا استعمال کرنے سے Z_\alpha=Z_{0.05}=1.645 ملتا ہے یعنی H_0 کو رد کریں اگر معلوم کیا گیا Z، −1.645 سے کم یا اس کے برابر ہو۔

vi. نتیجہ:

چونکہ Z کی ہماری معلوم کی گئی قیمت رد کے علاقے میں ہے، لہٰذا ہم H_0 رد کرتے ہیں اور H_1 قبول کرتے ہیں۔

sections.theory:
Example 7.3

Past records show that the average score of students in statistics is 57 with standard deviation 10. A new method of teaching is employed and a random sample of 70 students is selected. The sample average is 60. Can we conclude on the basis of these results, at 5% level of significance, that the average score has increased?

Solution:

i. H_0:\mu=57

H_1:\mu>57

ii. α = 5% = 0.05

iii. Test statistic: since σ is known, therefore, test statistic for μ in this case is Z=\frac{\overline{X}-\mu}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}}

iv. Calculation: Given that n = 70, \overline{X}=60, σ = 10, therefore,

$Z=\frac{60-57}{10/\sqrt{70}}=\frac{(3)\sqrt{70}}{10}=2.51$

v. Critical region:

As we see in H_1, we need to use one-sided test to the right. Here α = 0.05 (from the area table of S.N.D, we have Z_\alpha=Z_{0.05}=1.645).

sections.content:
Example 7.3

Past records show that the average score of students in statistics is 57 with standard deviation 10. A new method of teaching is employed and a random sample of 70 students is selected. The sample average is 60. Can we conclude on the basis of these results, at 5% level of significance, that the average score has increased?

Solution:

i. H_0:\mu=57

H_1:\mu>57

ii. α = 5% = 0.05

iii. Test statistic: since σ is known, therefore, test statistic for μ in this case is Z=\frac{\overline{X}-\mu}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}}

iv. Calculation: Given that n = 70, \overline{X}=60, σ = 10, therefore,

$Z=\frac{60-57}{10/\sqrt{70}}=\frac{(3)\sqrt{70}}{10}=2.51$

v. Critical region:

As we see in H_1, we need to use one-sided test to the right. Here α = 0.05 (from the area table of S.N.D, we have Z_\alpha=Z_{0.05}=1.645).
